narrative.overview:
The app is a binder. Sections are index tabs on the right edge, each with its own ink. Moving between pages turns a page. The pages themselves are black, and the work on them (checklists, card rows, label fields) sits on quiet graphite and slate. Neon is the binder's signage: the wordmark, the lit tab, the one button that moves you forward. It is not the wallpaper.

Because the people using it are both cataloguing at a desk and selling at a show table, the working surfaces are crisp and precise rather than playful. Dense lists, `text-sm` body, tight controls, keyboard-first. Personality comes from the wordmark, the glow and the voice of the copy, not from decorating the tools.

The app is dark-only. Paper is the one exception: labels, placeholder sheets and QR codes print black on white from their own isolated documents.
keyCharacteristics: Black page, graphite cards, slate wells: three dark steps, no light theme.
One neon hue per binder section, shown on the lit tab and its glow.
Neon fills always carry black ink.
The Neon display face appears only in the wordmark.
Index-tab navigation carries the binder metaphor; route changes are instant, with no page-turn transition.

rules.name: The Signage Rule
rules.body: Neon marks identity and action: the wordmark, the lit tab, the primary button, a status. Working surfaces stay black, graphite and slate. If a screen reads as "neon everywhere", something is decorating instead of signalling.

rules.name: The Black Ink Rule
rules.body: Text on a neon fill is always black. White on neon pink is 3.44:1 and on cyan 2.07:1; black is 6.1:1 or better on every hue. One ink keeps the buttons reading as one family.

rules.name: The One Hue Per Section Rule
rules.body: A section's colour is fixed by its tab (Dashboard green, Collection cyan, Inventory yellow, Admin amber, Print Shop teal, Profile violet). Don't borrow another section's hue for emphasis.

rules.name: The One Sign Rule
rules.body: The Neon face is the wordmark. It is never used for headings, buttons or body copy.

rules.name: The Four Weights Rule
rules.body: Lexend runs at 400 (body), 500 (labels, tabs), 600 (card and section titles) and 700 (page headings, numbers). Nothing lighter than 400, nothing heavier than 700.

rules.name: The Lit Means Active Rule
rules.body: A neon glow says "this is where you are" or "this is live". Never put a glow on a resting element for decoration.

rules.name: The Glow Not Fade Rule
rules.body: Neon text pulses its halo, never its opacity. `animate-pulse` on neon pink drops it to about 3:1 at the trough; the glow keeps the letters at full colour. One 12px halo, never stacked.

dos: **Do** put black ink on every neon fill.
**Do** keep each section in its tab's hue.
**Do** keep working surfaces on Page Black, Graphite and Slate Well, with neon only for signage and action.
**Do** dim disabled neon buttons to 45% opacity and honour `aria-disabled`.
**Do** give every dark input the Marquee Cyan focus ring.
**Do** print on white: print documents pin black on white and never load the app stylesheet.
donts: **Don't** use white text on neon pink, cyan or green.
**Don't** add a `prefers-color-scheme` rule or a light theme; the app is dark-only and the `dark:` variant keys off the `.dark` class.
**Don't** fade neon text with `animate-pulse`; pulse the glow instead.
**Don't** use the Neon display face anywhere but the wordmark.
**Don't** put a glow on a resting element.
**Don't** use neon pink for anything but cancel, destructive and sign-out.
